body_markdown:
**Cairo, November 19, 2026 –** The Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, Methanex Egypt, and the Engineering and Science Services (ESS) of the American University in Cairo (AUC) celebrated the graduation of the second and third cohorts of Egypt’s Process Safety Management (PSM) Professional Diploma, marking a key milestone in strengthening process safety capability and culture across the Egyptian oil, gas, and petrochemical sector.


With the graduation of its second and third cohorts, the AUC–Methanex PSM Professional Diploma has supported another 59 professionals from leading oil, gas, and petrochemical companies in strengthening their Process Safety Management capabilities. The four-month program comprises in-person and online learning, structured assessments, and applied projects to build a practical understanding of core PSM principles, enabling the graduates to apply these practices within their organizations and contribute to safer, more reliable operations across the Egyptian oil & gas and Petrochemicals sector.


The professional diploma was developed under the protocol signed in May 2025 between the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, AUC’s ESS, and Methanex Egypt, building on the 24 PSM standards and guidelines previously developed by the Ministry and Methanex and issued by the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation in 2022. Under this agreement, Methanex Egypt has committed to sponsoring 150 Ministry candidates over three years, with 91 professionals across three cohorts now successfully graduated and 32 candidates currently enrolled in the fourth cohort. Support will continue for the remaining cohorts, reinforcing long-term, sector-wide capability.


This diploma is the result of years of collaboration between the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and Methanex Egypt to embed PSM into the country’s oil, gas, and petrochemical sector, progressing from raising awareness, to establishing national PSM standards, and now to building professional capability for a safer future. Since 2018, this partnership has delivered tangible milestones including the development of 24 national PSM standards and guidelines, the launch of Egypt’s first official PSM website ([www.psmegypt.com](http://www.psmegypt.com/) ), the publication of the “Towards Safer Processes in the Oil, Gas and Petrochemical Industries” book, and the organization of multiple sector-wide PSM conference and knowledge sharing sessions. Together, these initiatives have laid the groundwork for stronger process safety culture and practices, positively impacting the industry and supporting a safer energy future for Egypt.
